review.summary: Attempt 3 is a genuinely additive, mechanically proven overlay. The one residual attempt-2 low is fixed: verify_typescript035_source.py now span-pins both new upstream declarations (length + SHA-256 + terminating semicolon) and derives their property key sets from that pinned text, and typescript035_profiles.py builds the two new graph nodes from those derived keys rather than a hand list. I independently confirmed the pinned source shapes, node/type reuse (s009588 catchall s009589, s009590/s009601), lossless typed-wins projection in generated.rs, the bounded default alias with the intact 23-binding denominator, frozen-byte preservation against baseline 578f2e6, and that all 107 recorded checks exit 0 on the reviewed SHA, including 906-case Zod↔Rust replay and both compilers. Two residual lows only.

findings.description: The synthesized ContentTypeConfiguration node indexes self.baseline['s009588']['properties'][key] with keys derived from the pinned 0.35.0 text. If a future re-pin names a protection key that is not present in the frozen 0.34.0 ModelConfiguration node, this raises a bare KeyError instead of one of the file's explicit domain errors ('Unreviewed TypeScript profile ancestor closure', 'Frozen profile root identity changed'). It fails closed, but the diagnostic is unactionable and inconsistent with the surrounding error vocabulary.
findings.required_fix: Check the derived key set against self.baseline['s009588']['properties'] and raise an explicit ValueError naming the unmatched key before building the node.

findings.description: The 906-case oracle replay compares Rust to Zod only in Mode::Request. For the six versioned clones that is deliberate (frozen tolerant responses are retained), but ContentTypeConfigurationSchema and ContentTypeConfigurationsSchema are brand-new roots with no frozen legacy, so their Mode::Response / Mode::ResponseWithoutDefaults acceptance is not compared against any oracle. Residual risk is small (format_inventory reports zero format sites in that closure and no defaults), but it is unexercised behavior on newly minted public schemas.
findings.required_fix: Replay the corpus for the two new roots in Mode::Response and Mode::ResponseWithoutDefaults as well, or record the Request-only bound explicitly in contracts/typescript-035-parity.json compatibility.

evidence: Attempt-2 finding resolved and tested: tools/verify_typescript035_source.py:13-35 pins ContentTypeConfigurationSchema (326 bytes, bd7bc799...) and ContentTypeConfigurationsSchema (343 bytes, 326ffb36...) by unique 'export const' anchor, re-hashes the exact span, requires the terminating semicolon, derives the four optional property keys from that text and requires exactly four unique keys plus a '.passthrough()' tail. tools/test_typescript035_source.py:42-58 asserts the derived key sets and, for each declaration, that deletion, duplication, .optional()->.nullable() and an inserted fifth property all fail with 'New profile declaration', and that line shifts are harmless.

Overlay now consumes the pinned text rather than a hand list: tools/typescript035_profiles.py:110-125 calls verify_new_profile_declarations and builds s_ts035_content_type_configuration from declarations['ContentTypeConfigurationSchema'] and s_ts035_content_type_configurations from declarations['ContentTypeConfigurationsSchema']. I verified the pinned upstream shapes directly at contracts/sources/typescript-0.35.0/src/models/mgmt-security-profile.ts:239-246 (four protection keys, passthrough) and :262-269 (prompt/response/tool-call/tool-response, passthrough), and that ModelConfigurationSchema (:272) is ContentTypeConfigurationSchema.extend, which is why copying s009588's four protection properties is the exact upstream shape.

Node reuse and metadata verified: tools/test_typescript035_profiles.py:147-168 asserts both new nodes are passthrough, share s009588's catchall {$ref: s009589} (ZodNever), that each copied property equals the frozen s009588 property, that every property carries inputPresence 'accepts'/inputNull 'rejects', the exact direction key set, that directions reference s_ts035_configuration_optional, and that no new node carries vendorProjection.

Additivity proven against the Git baseline, not asserted: tools/test_typescript035_implementation.py:112-127 asserts every historical schema_graph node and root survives byte-identically, that added nodes are exactly the 12 clones plus 4 new nodes and added roots exactly 8, and that the committed graph equals Overlay.extend_graph(baseline); :140-148 asserts contracts/native-models.json 'schemas', 'modelExports', 'unionVariantPins' and 'aliases' are byte-equal to 578f2e6 with only two supplemental rows added; :37-53 proves contracts/native-fixtures/schemas.json differs from baseline only in provenance.generatorSha256 and crates/scm-sdk/src/fixtures/model-regressions.json only in provenance.sha256/oracleSha256, each bound to current bytes. tools/typescript035_profiles.py:267-282 (--check) independently reconstructs the committed graph from the committed graph minus the overlay.

Lossless typed-wins projection uses the pre-existing mechanism (tools/generate_models.py:471-506, which rejects a non-optional projection and excludes projection keys from KNOWN): generated.rs:4467-4512 removes 'content-type-mode'/'content-type-configurations', and on decode failure re-inserts the raw value as an extension; :4539-4556 emits the typed value and skips a same-key extension only when the typed field is set. Same pattern at :14523 (SecurityProfile dlp_tenant_id), :153638 (ModelConfiguration enable_full_conversation_inspection) and :168370 (CreateSecurityProfileRequest dlp_tenant_id) — exactly the five planned occurrences, confirmed by grep across generated.rs (the Patch<bool> hits at :22670/:23310 are unrelated Red Team scan models).

New public types are ordinary generated models: generated.rs:13369-13477 and :13490-13593 give both types derive(Clone, PartialEq, Deserialize), non_exhaustive, flattened Extensions, redacted Debug, SCHEMA/parse/builder/build_validated, and a collision guard on known keys; crates/scm-sdk/src/models/management.rs:9-10 re-exports both types and builders in airs::management.

Bounded default alias: tools/generate_validation.py:14 (header import) and :151-154 refuse an alias whose original is not exactly {binding: default, default: []}; tools/response_defaults.py:60-78,117-120 re-checks the alias root (typescript:0.35.0:SecurityProfileListResponseSchema -> s_ts035_s009651) and its ai_profiles field, records it separately in contracts/response-defaults.json:498-506 and still asserts the 23-binding denominator (counts at :18-20); crates/scm-sdk/src/validation/tests.rs:206-220 asserts semantics.len()==70 with [] inserted under Mode::Response and omitted under ResponseWithoutDefaults. crates/scm-sdk/src/validation/semantics.json contains exactly one s_ts035 entry.

Oracle integrity and isolation: tools/typescript035-oracle.mts:19 runs the source verifier before any copy, :22-25 pins Zod to the committed lockfile, :34 substitutes the DLP identifier with placeholder '100', :194-225 executes in a disposable .local workspace it then removes. tools/test_typescript035_oracle.py:73-86 proves a tampered model file and a tampered manifest both fail before execution with no UPSTREAM_EXECUTED marker and no workspace; :88-105 proves a doctored corpus and a changed script fail without rewriting bytes; :38-71 proves determinism, source immutability and specific nested rejections.

Executed Zod/Rust equivalence: crates/scm-sdk/tests/typescript035_models.rs:44-87 replays every corpus case through validation::parse (versioned roots for the six clones, plain names for the two new schemas), compares acceptance and normalized output, typed-round-trips each root and requires at least one acceptance and one rejection per root; :91-110 covers omission/null/unsupported response JSON for all five projections in both response modes. docs/checks/phase-27-rust-1.89.0-management.json:90 records all four typescript035_models tests, the four directional management_contracts wire tests and all_23_frozen_defaults passing, with fmt/check/clippy -D warnings/test/examples/doc and the directional_profiles example at exit 0; the same set is recorded for 1.99.0 (checks.json:3013).

Check evidence is source-bound and complete: docs/reviews/phase-27-chunk-models-and-validation-attempt-03.checks.json records source_sha256 85e6533f... (the reviewed SHA), source_unchanged true, passed true, and 107 invocations executed in one continuous run 08:50:37-09:07:28Z. A regex scan for any exit_code other than 0, any timeout true, or any source_unchanged false returned no matches. Key recorded outputs: typescript035_profiles.py --check {addedExports 4, addedModels 2, addedSchemas 2, projectedFields 5, versionedRoots 6, clonedNodes 12, defaultAliases 1} (:2871), typescript035-oracle.mts --check {roots 8, cases 906, accepted 231} (:2911), generate_models.py --check {outputs 20, graphNodes 13018} (:1941), verify-contracts.py --self-test with 29 rejected tamper cases including modified-supplemental-source (:119).

Narrow, justified oracle adapter change: tools/schema-oracle.mts:242-249 retains the original discriminator optionsMap and adapts only the mapped children, with the ESM/CommonJS rationale in-comment; request schemas untouched. tools/test_schema_oracle.py:12-48 extracts the actual adapter and executes it across two distinct Zod module identities, proves z.discriminatedUnion rebuild throws, and checks dispatch, enum widening, unknown-key passthrough and six rejection cases. tools/test_model_fixtures.py:19-32 verifies the current generatorSha256 binding before normalizing to the historical pin ddc0f2ac... .

Ownership and scope integrity: contracts/typescript-035-parity.json:7-18 binds SHA-256 for the pinned model file, both generators, the verifier, profiles.rs, the wire tests, the model test and the example; tools/verify-contracts.py:133-143,492 delegates the supplemental source inventory to its owner and fails closed on the owner's exception (tools/test_typescript035_source.py:109-115). docs/phase-status.json:6870-6999 chunk scope_evidence matches the reviewed chunk scope exactly and its latest scope_revision.
limitations: Read-only Read/Glob/Grep only: I could not recompute the SHA-256 of the reviewed source or of the checks artifact, nor re-execute any check, test, generator or oracle. Pass/fail conclusions rest on the recorded commands, exit codes, stdout/stderr and executed_at values in the attempt-03 checks artifact, cross-read against the artifacts they claim to own.
I read no credential or tenant-registration files, used no .local/typescript checkout, and made no network calls.

schema_graph.json and semantics.json are single-line minified artifacts; I verified their new roots, nodes and the single s_ts035 semantic entry by targeted grep plus the generator reconstruction path and the Python/Rust regressions, not by reading them end to end.

Oracle-to-Rust comparison is Mode::Request only (see finding 2); I did not independently recount the 906 corpus cases, relying on the recorded --check byte-equality run and the Rust replay's per-root acceptance/rejection assertions.

Wire-chunk artifacts (profiles.rs, management_contracts.rs, the example, CHANGELOG/STABILITY/DIRECTIONAL_PROFILES, check_phase.py) were read only insofar as they evidence this chunk's claims; they are scored under wire-and-compatibility. Phase 27 deliberately defers clean extracted package-consumer checks to phase 28.

Live/service acceptance for directional profiles remains explicitly unestablished (contracts/typescript-035-parity.json compatibility.liveAcceptance); I did not assess it, nor re-audit historical phase 19-24 infrastructure, release receipts or the frozen 0.34.0 baseline beyond the identity checks this overlay depends on.
